text:
Alex: CI turned red on my feature branch after merging main — failing one unit test only on linux-fast job. Anyone seen TestTokenizer::handles-edge-cases fail recently? build: https://ci.redwood.com/teams/eng/builds/98765

Alex: ```
FAIL: TestTokenizer::handles-edge-cases
Expected: ['😀', 'a']
Actual:   ['😀a']
AssertionError: token boundaries differ
Stack: tokenizer/tests/test_tokenizer.py:42
```

Jamie: Hmm, saw similar flake on main yesterday but it passed on rerun. Can you paste full job log or job id?

Alex: job_id=98765-12, pasted the short log above. Rebased earlier today onto main and resolved conflicts in pyproject.lock — CI still failing.

Taylor: There's been a small emoji-normalization change in the tokenization PR (linked in #3129). If you rebased after that it could flip behavior. Did you re-run the tests locally?

Alex: Ran pytest locally in docker image (ubuntu-22.04) and it passes for me. CI uses linux-fast image with system libicu v72 — could be env-dependent.

Morgan: I can bisect if needed. Can someone kick a rerun while I grab the repo? @ci-bot rerun build 98765 job 12

ci-bot: Rerun queued for build 98765 job 12 — estimated start in ~1 min. (Triggered by Morgan) :gear:

Jamie: If it's flaky, try the focused test job to save cycles: `./scripts/ci/run_test.sh tokenizer::TestTokenizer::handles-edge-cases` — that reproduces the CI harness locally.

Alex: Ran that exact command in a clean container and it passed. Weird.

ci-bot: Rerun started — https://ci.redwood.com/teams/eng/builds/98765/runs/13

ci-bot: Build finished — FAILURE (linux-fast)

Taylor: Okay it failed again. Two hypotheses: (1) environment difference (libicu), (2) test relies on nondeterministic normalization order. If Morgan can bisect, we can pin the commit that introduced the change.

Morgan: Starting git bisect now. Can you confirm the minimal repro command and the branch name?

Alex: Branch: feature/embed-token-fixes. Repro: `git checkout feature/embed-token-fixes && ./scripts/ci/run_test.sh tokenizer::TestTokenizer::handles-edge-cases` — run inside docker image `eng/ci:linux-fast`

Morgan: Got it. I'll run bisect on CI-equivalent image and update here. Expect ~30-40 runs.

Jamie: One other quick option: revert the merge commit temporarily and run CI to see if the merge caused it. That’s faster if we can afford a revert.

Alex: I don't want to block the branch; bisect sounds better. Thanks for doing that.

Morgan: Update: bisect narrowed it to commit 33f4a7d — "emoji boundary: normalize extended grapheme clusters". That matches the tokenization change Taylor mentioned.

Taylor: Yup that's the PR. The change was intentional to match spec but it looks like the test expected old behavior. We should update the test to accept either boundary or adjust tokenizer to preserve previous case for legacy API.

Alex: I'll open a fix PR to relax the assertion to allow both unicode escape forms and the normalized emoji char. Will run CI after.

Morgan: Posting quick patch idea in #pr-drafts. If you want, I can push a hotfix branch and run a targeted CI job to unblock you faster.

Alex: That would be great — thanks. If CI passes after fix, we can merge and close this thread.

Jamie: Also adding a short note to the changelog about tokenization spec change so other tests can be checked.

Alex: Fix PR created: https://git.redwood.com/redwood/infra/pull/3167. Running focused CI now.

ci-bot: Build queued (focused tests) — https://ci.redwood.com/teams/eng/builds/98801

ci-bot: Build finished — SUCCESS :tada:

Alex: Merged the fix into my branch and CI is green now. Thanks everyone for quick help :thumbsup:

Taylor: Nice work. I'll follow up with a small eval to ensure no behavior regressions for downstream tokenizers.

Morgan: Closing bisect — culprit confirmed and test adjusted.

Alex: Closing thread. Cheers!
